job_title: Accounting, finance, banking, insurance Jobs in Kenya
company: Description Key Responsibilities 1. Project Financial Management Manage the financial aspects of assigned projects throughout the project lifecycle, from proposal development to project close-out Ensure project expenditure is correctly budgeted, coded, authorized, recorded and supported by appropriate documentation. Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and identify significant variances, risks, and funding gaps. Provide financial advice to Project Managers and program teams on project implementation and expenditure. Ensure project funds are used efficiently and in accordance with donor and organizational requirements. Monitor staff, partner and project advances and ensure timely liquidation and reconciliation. 2. Budgeting and Forecasting Lead the development of project budgets in collaboration with Program/Project Managers. Review project budgets to ensure they are realistic, complete, and aligned with program activities and donor requirements. Prepare monthly/quarterly project forecasts and cash-flow projections. Conduct budget-versus-actual analysis and provide explanations and recommendations for significant variances. Support budget revisions, reallocations, and other financial changes required during project implementation. Support annual organizational and departmental budgeting. 3. Donor Financial Management and Compliance Ensure compliance with donor financial rules, grant agreements and approved project budgets. Prepare and/or review donor financial reports and ensure timely submission. Maintain a clear record of donor financial requirements, reporting deadlines, and budget restrictions. Review donor contracts and agreements from a financial perspective and advise management of financial risks and obligations. Respond to donor financial queries and support donor audits. Ensure project expenditure is eligible, allowable, reasonable, and adequately documented. 4. Financial Reporting and Analysis Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual project financial reports. Prepare budget-versus-actual reports and variance analysis for management and Project Managers. Provide financial information for management, donor, Board and audit reporting. Analyze project expenditure, burn rates, forecasts, and financial performance. Develop and maintain financial dashboards and management reports where required. Provide timely financial information to support program decision-making. 5. Financial Controls and Risk Management Ensure effective financial controls are implemented across projects and organizational operations. Monitor compliance with financial policies, procedures, and delegated authorities. Identify financial, fraud and compliance risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures. Ensure proper segregation of duties and adequate supporting documentation. Follow up financial control weaknesses and audit recommendations. Promote accountability, transparency, and value for money across all projects. 6. Partner Financial Management Where projects are implemented through partners: Participate in financial due diligence and capacity assessments of implementing partners. Review partner budgets and financial reports. Monitor partner expenditure and advances. Conduct financial monitoring and spot checks as required. Identify financial control weaknesses and follow up on corrective actions. Provide financial management training and support to partners where required. 7. Accounting and Treasury Oversight Oversee accounts payable, accounts receivable, and general ledger processes. Review KES and foreign currency bank reconciliations, MPESA reconciliations, and other account reconciliations. Monitor cash requirements and prepare cash-flow forecasts. Oversee accruals, prepayments, journal entries, and month-end/year-end closing. Ensure proper management of fixed assets, inventory, and the fixed asset register. Ensure accurate and complete financial records and audit trails are maintained. 8. Statutory Compliance Ensure timely preparation, reconciliation and submission of applicable statutory returns and payments, including PAYE, NSSF, SHIF, VAT, withholding tax and instalment tax. Liaise with relevant statutory authorities to resolve financial and tax matters. Monitor changes in relevant financial and tax requirements and advise management accordingly. 9. Audit and Project Close-Out Coordinate project and organizational financial audits. Prepare audit schedules and support documentation. Respond to audit queries and follow up on implementation of audit recommendations. Lead the financial aspects of project close-out, including reconciliation of expenditure, advances, assets, commitments and final donor financial reports. Ensure project financial records are complete and properly archived. 10. Capacity Building and Financial Business Partnering Build the financial management capacity of Project Managers and program staff. Train non-finance staff on budgeting, financial procedures, donor compliance, and budget monitoring. Support program teams to understand and use financial information for decision-making. Promote a culture of financial accountability across the organization. Identify opportunities to improve financial systems, processes, reporting, and automation. Key Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration or related field. Professional qualifications such as CPA(K), ACCA, or equivalent . At least 5 years' relevant professional experience , preferably in an NGO, international development or donor-funded organization. Demonstrated experience in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and budget monitoring. Experience with donor-funded projects and donor compliance. Strong knowledge of Kenyan statutory and tax requirements. Experience in financial audits, internal controls, and risk management. Strong Excel, financial analysis skills, and experience using accounting/ERP systems.

company: Description THE ORGANISATION Finlays is a leading independent business-to-business supplier of tea, coffee and botanical solutions to beverage brand owners worldwide. job_title: Information technology, software development, data Jobs for Senior-level in Kenya
company: Description You will build software that safely and securely moves billions of dollars to millions of vulnerable people in some of the poorest and highest need parts of the world. This will require applying excellent engineering, team building and organizational judgment to complex, high-stakes operations: identity and fraud management, machine learning on large but imperfect datasets (cell phone data, satellite imagery, government registries), mobile money integrations, low-connectivity environments, rapidly evolving requirements all in diverse regulatory environments and country contexts. You’ll need to keep our legacy technology stack stable and performant, while in parallel building new systems from the ground up for our next level of scale. You will lead engineering, data, security and enterprise technology – with a small, mighty and rapidly growing engineering team of ~15, and the expectation that this can at least double to ~30 in the next 12 months if you want it to. You’ll report to a CEO with deep experience running technology companies, and partner with our VP Product. What we’re looking for: An exceptional hirer, manager and organizer of technical talent. Proven record identifying, hiring, developing and retaining excellent engineers and engineering leaders, and creating team processes that consistently deliver software with quality and velocity. Deep technical judgment, applied close to the work. You can evaluate major designs, pressure-test architecture and build-vs-buy decisions, and recognize when a team is heading the wrong way, without becoming the primary implementer. Low-ego: you’ll investigate a problem yourself when that’s what the situation requires. Business judgment and decisiveness under ambiguity. You’re not just a technical leader, you’re also a business executive. You understand the business, are a strong cross-functional partner, and have a history of good judgment when navigating tradeoffs of long vs. short term, speed, reliability, security, flexibility, cost, technical quality, and user impact. AI first. You have a point of view on where AI meaningfully changes engineering productivity and organizational capability, and you’ve moved a team from experimentation to real, measured use. You can set the tools, culture, goals, and guardrails that leverage the opportunities and mitigate the risks of an AI first engineering culture. Embody and set an example for GD values. We take our values incredibly seriously, and expect our leaders to embody, nurture, and promote them in the way they work and the teams they build. Advantages, not requirements. Experience in an operationally complex or regulated domain (fintech, payments, humanitarian response, global development); systems involving financial controls, fraud risk, identity, or sensitive recipient data; operating across multiple countries, particularly lower-income or infrastructure-constrained ones; leading both modern product engineering and enterprise technology. What you’ll do Define our technology vision and target stack. Own the technical strategy for technology-first delivery at $5B+/year: architecture, platforms, build-vs-buy, and what we retire. Work with executive, product, finance, risk, and data leaders to turn program and product strategy into a sequenced, credible portfolio of technical investments. Balance a demanding portfolio. You’ll manage six workstreams that all matter and won’t all move at once: (1) building our new cash delivery stack (remote-first verification, fraud prevention, massive volume) (2) stabilizing our legacy stack until switchover, then managing the migration; (3) donor-facing fundraising products; (4) our global emergency cash system (and eventual white-labelling of that product); (5) enterprise technology; (6) internal tooling, platform, and cybersecurity. Deciding sequencing and staffing across these (and saying “not yet” credibly) is the job. Build and grow an exceptional technology organization. Recruit outstanding engineering and technology talent, design the org GiveDirectly needs at its next stage of scale (engineering, product, data, security, infrastructure, enterprise systems), and create the accountability, decision rights, and career paths to sustain high talent density. Grow the engineering team from 15 to ~30 with a lean but durable management structure. Own the technical direction and quality bar. Guide consequential decisions on integrations, data, security, reliability, and technical debt. Ensure our systems can safely support a major increase in transaction volume, geographic reach, and organizational dependence on technology. Set a pragmatic quality bar appropriate to high-stakes financial delivery while preserving speed. Lead across organizational boundaries. Serve as a member of GiveDirectly’s executive team, reporting to the CEO and bringing technology into major strategic and operating decisions. Help non-technical leaders understand technical constraints and costs, build credibility with country and functional leaders by understanding their realities, and force clarity when priorities, ownership, or tradeoffs are ambiguous. Travel. Approximately 4–6 trips per year, including visits to GiveDirectly countries of operation. Technical Evaluation of Electrical Equipment • Understand and evaluate the technical capacity, ratings, and specifications of MV panels/switchgear (11kV/33kV VCB, RMU), LV panels (MCCB/ACB distribution boards), and power/distribution transformers (dry-type and oil-filled). • Assess vendor technical offers against project specifications, IEC/BS/KS (KEBS) standards, and approved benchmark equipment, flagging non-compliances. • Support selection of lighting fixtures based on lux level requirements, IP/IK ratings, lumen output, and compliance with the project's Schedule of Light Fittings. • Apply correct cable selection principles — sizing based on current rating, voltage drop, derating factors, cable type (XLPE/PVC, armoured/unarmoured), and application (LV/MV, fire-rated, control). • Prepare and maintain technical compliance/comparison workbooks (vendor-vs-approved benchmark) for panels, transformers, cables, and lighting submissions. 3. Procurement, Vendor Management & Negotiation • Source and shortlist vendors/manufacturers for electrical materials and equipment (panels, transformers, cables, lighting, accessories) locally and internationally (India, China, UAE, South Africa, Europe). • Issue RFQs/enquiries, collect and technically screen vendor quotations, and prepare vendor comparison summaries for management/MD approval. • Negotiate pricing, payment terms, lead times, and warranty/after-sales terms directly with vendors and suppliers to achieve best commercial value without compromising technical compliance. • Track and evaluate vendor performance, certification validity (type-test certificates, PVOC, ISO), and reliability for future sourcing decisions. • Generate Local Purchase Orders (LPOs) and procurement documentation using MPSL's standard templates, ensuring accuracy of quantities, rates, and specifications. 4. Estimation & Cost Control • Prepare material cost estimates and pricing schedules for tenders, variations, and value- engineering (VE) proposals. • Maintain and update price trackers, material trackers, and BOQ-vs-order tracking tools to prevent over-ordering and control project costs. • Support Value Engineering exercises (e.g., alternative equipment configurations, 'or-equal' substitutions) with clear technical and cost justification. 5. Procurement & Commercial Skills • 2-3 years of hands-on experience in electrical procurement and/or estimation, preferably within an MEP contracting or construction environment. • Demonstrated experience preparing vendor comparisons, negotiating pricing/terms, and closing purchase orders. • Strong command of MS Excel (formulas, trackers, comparison sheets) and MS Word for technical/commercial documentation. • Good communication skills for vendor negotiation and cross-functional coordination with project teams. Preferred / Added Advantage • Prior exposure to East African market suppliers and import/logistics processes (Kenya, Uganda). • Experience working on institutional/hospital or UN/international-standard projects. • Knowledge of PVOC and other Kenya/Uganda import compliance requirements. Prepare and maintain quality documentation, including SOPs, inspection checklists, audit reports and non-conformance reports (NCRs). Liaise with clients, IRATA, certification bodies and regulatory authorities during audits, inspections and certification renewals. Track and report quality KPIs (e.g. audit pass rates, non-conformance trends, rework rates) to senior management. Support recruitment and onboarding by verifying candidate certifications, licences and competency records before deployment to site. Maintain accurate document control and record-keeping for all quality-related certifications, licences and permits. Coordinate with HSE personnel to align quality and safety compliance programmes. Keep up to date with evolving IRATA standards, ISO requirements and applicable national and international regulatory changes. QUALIFICATIONS & CERTIFICATIONS Diploma or Degree in Quality Management, Engineering, Occupational Health & Safety, or a related field. Recognised quality control/quality assurance certification required — e.g. ISO 9001 Lead Auditor/Internal Auditor, ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) or Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or equivalent. Demonstrated experience conducting audits, developing and maintaining quality procedures, and ensuring compliance with applicable quality standards and regulatory requirements. Experience working with IRATA member companies or within height-safety environments is highly desirable but not essential. Working familiarity with permit-to-work systems, RAMS and method statements. SKILLS & COMPETENCIES Strong working knowledge of applicable quality standards (e.g. ISO 9001, IRATA ICOP) and relevant regulatory requirements. Excellent attention to detail with strong analytical and root-cause analysis skills. Strong report-writing, documentation and record-keeping skills. Good communication (English, Swahili) and interpersonal skills, able to liaise confidently with technicians, management and clients. Ensure project funds are used efficiently and in accordance with donor and organizational requirements. Monitor staff, partner and project advances and ensure timely liquidation and reconciliation. 2. Budgeting and Forecasting Lead the development of project budgets in collaboration with Program/Project Managers. Review project budgets to ensure they are realistic, complete, and aligned with program activities and donor requirements. Prepare monthly/quarterly project forecasts and cash-flow projections. Conduct budget-versus-actual analysis and provide explanations and recommendations for significant variances. Support budget revisions, reallocations, and other financial changes required during project implementation. Support annual organizational and departmental budgeting. 3. Donor Financial Management and Compliance Ensure compliance with donor financial rules, grant agreements and approved project budgets. Prepare and/or review donor financial reports and ensure timely submission. Maintain a clear record of donor financial requirements, reporting deadlines, and budget restrictions. Review donor contracts and agreements from a financial perspective and advise management of financial risks and obligations. Respond to donor financial queries and support donor audits. Ensure project expenditure is eligible, allowable, reasonable, and adequately documented. 4. Financial Reporting and Analysis Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual project financial reports. Prepare budget-versus-actual reports and variance analysis for management and Project Managers. Provide financial information for management, donor, Board and audit reporting. Analyze project expenditure, burn rates, forecasts, and financial performance. Develop and maintain financial dashboards and management reports where required. Provide timely financial information to support program decision-making. 5. Financial Controls and Risk Management Ensure effective financial controls are implemented across projects and organizational operations. Monitor compliance with financial policies, procedures, and delegated authorities. Identify financial, fraud and compliance risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures. Ensure proper segregation of duties and adequate supporting documentation. Follow up financial control weaknesses and audit recommendations. Promote accountability, transparency, and value for money across all projects. 6. Partner Financial Management Where projects are implemented through partners: Participate in financial due diligence and capacity assessments of implementing partners. Review partner budgets and financial reports. Monitor partner expenditure and advances. Conduct financial monitoring and spot checks as required. Identify financial control weaknesses and follow up on corrective actions. Provide financial management training and support to partners where required. 7. Accounting and Treasury Oversight Oversee accounts payable, accounts receivable, and general ledger processes. Review KES and foreign currency bank reconciliations, MPESA reconciliations, and other account reconciliations. Monitor cash requirements and prepare cash-flow forecasts. Oversee accruals, prepayments, journal entries, and month-end/year-end closing. Ensure proper management of fixed assets, inventory, and the fixed asset register. Ensure accurate and complete financial records and audit trails are maintained. 8. Statutory Compliance Ensure timely preparation, reconciliation and submission of applicable statutory returns and payments, including PAYE, NSSF, SHIF, VAT, withholding tax and instalment tax. Liaise with relevant statutory authorities to resolve financial and tax matters. Monitor changes in relevant financial and tax requirements and advise management accordingly. 9. Audit and Project Close-Out Coordinate project and organizational financial audits. Prepare audit schedules and support documentation. Respond to audit queries and follow up on implementation of audit recommendations. Lead the financial aspects of project close-out, including reconciliation of expenditure, advances, assets, commitments and final donor financial reports. Ensure project financial records are complete and properly archived. 10. Capacity Building and Financial Business Partnering Build the financial management capacity of Project Managers and program staff. Train non-finance staff on budgeting, financial procedures, donor compliance, and budget monitoring. Support program teams to understand and use financial information for decision-making. Promote a culture of financial accountability across the organization. Identify opportunities to improve financial systems, processes, reporting, and automation. Key Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration or related field. Professional qualifications such as CPA(K), ACCA, or equivalent . At least 5 years' relevant professional experience , preferably in an NGO, international development or donor-funded organization. Demonstrated experience in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and budget monitoring. Experience with donor-funded projects and donor compliance. Strong knowledge of Kenyan statutory and tax requirements. Experience in financial audits, internal controls, and risk management. Strong Excel, financial analysis skills, and experience using accounting/ERP systems.

company: Description Job Summary For this role, The Driver will be responsible for providing safe, reliable, and timely transportation for staff, visitors, equipment, and other organizational needs. This role will also involve maintaining the assigned vehicle in good condition, ensuring proper documentation, supporting field activities, and assisting with logistics and transportation-related tasks as required. Key Responsibilities: General Duties Provide reliable and safe driving services ensuring high accuracy of work and timeliness. Demonstrate a high sense of responsibility, courtesy, tact, and the ability to work with people of different national and cultural backgrounds. Provide driving services to the operations and staff in the Country Projects and visiting experts. Responsible for driving office vehicles for the transport of authorized personnel and delivery and collection of mail, documents, and other items. Ensure cost-saving through proper use of vehicle through accurate maintenance of daily vehicle logs, provision of inputs to preparation of vehicle maintenance plans and reports. Ensure proper day-to-day maintenance of the assigned vehicle through timely minor repairs, arrangements for major repairs, timely changes of oil, check of tires, brakes, car washing, etc. Ensure availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, vehicle logs, office directory, map of the city/country, first aid kit, necessary spare parts. Ensure that all immediate actions required by rules and regulations are taken in case of involvement in accidents. Operations Accurately register patients in Outreaches and record accurate and clear records of patients. Oversee an organized general patient flow in an eye camp in partnership with the Community Health Volunteers or otherwise mobilizers. Take detailed medical histories that include current and past prescriptions. Educate and advise patients on proper eye care while maintaining high standard of care. Ensure the patient’s Registration queues are well organized and sequential. Perform any other tasks or duties as assigned by the Executive Director or other senior leadership, as required by the evolving needs of the organization and the context in which it operates. Qualifications & Skills: Minimum 5 years of professional driving experience. Must have a valid Kenyan driving license with the appropriate class for driving a van. Must have a valid PSV (Public Service Vehicle) license. KCSE certificate or equivalent qualification. Clean driving record and strong commitment to road safety. Good knowledge of Nairobi and major routes across Kenya. Basic knowledge of vehicle maintenance and troubleshooting. Good communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently, manage time effectively, and follow instructions. Professional, reliable, punctual, and trustworthy. Ability to maintain confidentiality when handling staff and organizational information. First Aid certification or basic first aid knowledge would be an added advantage. NB: Interviews are on a rolling basis. Only short-listed candidate (s) will be contacted. GoodVision Kenya is an equal opportunity employer, and respect all gender, nationality or religious affiliations.
